html:
The cube-shaped stone building at the centre of the Great Mosque in Mecca, the holiest site in Islam. Muslims everywhere face it when they pray, and pilgrims walk around it seven times.

Muslim tradition says it was first built by Abraham and his son Ishmael as a house for the one God. Before Islam it was a shrine for the tribes of Arabia and held their idols. About 605 the people of Mecca rebuilt it after a flood, and the young Muhammad is said to have set the Black Stone in its corner. In 630, when he took Mecca, he cleared the idols out.

It has been rebuilt several times since: after sieges in 683 and 692, and after a flood in 1630 under the Ottomans. It stands about 13 metres high and is covered by the kiswa, a black silk cloth embroidered in gold that is replaced each year.
sum: The cube-shaped stone building at the centre of the Great Mosque in Mecca, the holiest site in Islam. Muslims everywhere face it when they pray, and pilgrims walk around it seven times.
